BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every liability and risk-allocation point. Several positions are presented as "agreed" or "settled" when they are not. The Disclosure Letter, read carefully, actually helps us: it candidly admits that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment and the bonus funding are all unresolved. We should use those admissions.

---

## A. Liability regime – reject and re-mark

| Point | Seller draft | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **12.1 General cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | 20% is our *conditional fallback* only. No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given identifying this draft, so we have **no authority to accept it**. Revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m. |
| **12.2 De minimis** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. Revert. |
| **12.2 Basket** | AUD 250,000, **excess-only** (deductible) | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar** (tipping) | 5x our figure and the wrong mechanic. Together with the de minimis, a deductible basket at this level would absorb most realistic warranty claims on a AUD 24m deal. Revert on both amount and mechanic. |
| **12.3/13 Claims period** | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval; none given. Revert to 24 months. |
| **13 "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Any limitation applies to all Claims by default | Keep categories separate; no hidden override | **Reject outright.** This single sentence would sweep Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities (Ironquay), payment and covenant claims into the 20% cap, 18-month period and deductible basket. It is the most important drafting issue in the package. Replace with the reverse default: limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. |
| **Fundamental/Title** | Same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject. Title to the shares is the entire consideration; capping it at 20% is unacceptable. Insist on the separate regime. |
| **9.3/12.8/20.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature"** | Universal | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of everything; indemnities and other categories separate | Reject. As drafted, fraud would be capped and time-barred. Insert an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. Confirm specific indemnities and Tax/IP sit outside 9.3/12.8/20.5. |

## B. Disclosure and knowledge – the two provisions that would gut the warranties

**Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]:** Seller deems the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), statutory registers and public records disclosed. Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Require *specific fair disclosure* – facts disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter – against identified warranties. Note [1.4] (non-admission of any requirement for consent, payment, notice etc.) is unobjectionable in itself but confirms the Seller is not accepting any obligation on the open items; we must impose those obligations by covenant/condition, not rely on the letter.

**8.3 Buyer knowledge:** Blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew *or could have discovered* from the data room or public records. Delete. Combined with [1.1], this would mean nothing in the data room could ever ground a claim – effectively no warranty protection on the diligenced items at all. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be: actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, not constructive/"discoverable"; and it must never apply to Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. Correspondingly, seller "awareness" qualifiers must be tied to named seller persons after reasonable enquiry.

## C. Conditions and completion mechanics – real deal risk

**Bluefen (3/6.3):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Disclosure Letter [2] admits no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and deems consent satisfied "on delivery of written consent." Reject both: reasonable endeavours is inadequate for a material customer consent, and delivery of a consent letter is not the same as an *effective* consent with its 11.3 conditions met. Make it a condition precedent: effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied, evidenced) Bluefen consent before Completion, with a Buyer right to waive only in writing.

**Riverlark (2/7):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; [3] admits no repayment and no discharge. A post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company encumbered in favour of a lender, with debt-free/cash-free pricing. Require: current payout letter; repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed security releases/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release structure requires an irrevocable lender undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval – neither exists.

**Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and omitted from the funds flow; [5] admits on-costs (super, payroll tax) are unaddressed. On a debt-free/cash-free deal, an omitted Completion-triggered liability is a silent price increase to us. Require either a specific funds-flow line item (gross of on-costs) deducted from the price, or a Seller covenant/indemnity to fund them, with the figure confirmed by the Company's payroll. Confirm the continued-employment conditions and who bears the cost if conditions fail post-Completion.

## D. Specific risk items

**Ironquay IP (11.1):** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; [4] confirms no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way – we should not assume it is unpaid, nor accept it is paid. Position: (i) preserve the cure – Seller to procure cleared payment and a confirmatory IP assignment/receipt as a Completion deliverable; (ii) broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment itself to cover any failure of title to the Project Materials, third-party claims, re-procurement and remediation costs; (iii) indemnity sits outside the general cap, basket and claims period.

**DD-006 export/privacy incident (4.6/Sch 6):** ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; [6] confirms the investigation is preliminary and access, scope and notification duty are unknown. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a characterisation, not a finding; equally we have no basis to assert a confirmed breach, harm or notification duty, and should not quantify. Position: interim covenants to preserve logs/evidence, complete the investigation, provide updates and copies of any regulator/third-party correspondence before Completion; a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident (uncapped by the general regime, or at least separately capped); and a bring-down warranty at Completion. Do not treat it as a price item at this stage.

**Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000):** Seller says ordinary course; [8] admits it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Assess rather than assert: obtain the renewal terms, timing and termination rights. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction per playbook, but reserve the position pending that information and consider a working-capital/accrual treatment if they are committed.

**Tax / IP:** Seller says "settled under the general regime." They are **not** settled – both remain OPEN on our side. Reject the characterisation in writing so silence is not taken as acceptance. We are not seeking unlimited liability, but Tax and IP must be separate categories outside the 20%/18-month general regime, with their own cap and period (Tax at least aligned to assessment periods).

**Title (DD-012):** The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register, and [10] admits the Buyer has not completed its own verification. An internal register is a supplied source, not independent proof. Require: current ASIC company extract, constitution, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller's shares, Seller board resolutions/authority, share certificates, and a search for options/convertibles/encumbrances. Title/authority warranties under the Fundamental regime.

**Minor:** DD-007 lease – confirm the landlord notification is given on or before Completion and no consent is triggered. DD-009 Mossvale – confirm by reading the clause that there is no change-of-control trigger; if ambiguous, seek comfort or a warranty.

---

## E. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

1. **Strike the cross-cutting overrides** – cl 13 "applies to all Claims" default, and 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature." Reverse the default; carve out fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct non-waivably; keep Fundamental, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant claims outside the general regime.
2. **Revert the general regime** to 25% / AUD 6.0m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket; 24 months. Note internally that no authority exists for the 20% or 18-month fallbacks.
3. **Fundamental/Title**: separate regime – 100% cap, six years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar – plus independent title evidence.
4. **Delete cl 8.3** and reject general data-room/public-record disclosure; require specific fair disclosure.
5. **Bluefen**: effective consent with 11.3 conditions evidenced as a condition precedent, not endeavours/deemed satisfaction.
6. **Riverlark**: payout, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion.
7. **Bonuses**: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded.
8. **Ironquay**: broadened indemnity outside the general regime; cleared payment and confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.
9. **DD-006**: preservation, investigation and update covenants; specific indemnity; no numbers asserted either way.
10. **Tax/IP**: reject "settled"; remain open as separate categories.
11. **Sandbar**: request information; no concession on classification yet.

One drafting caution for the response letter: the Seller's cover note and cl 13 frame positions as "agreed"/"negotiated." Our mark-up should expressly state that nothing is agreed save as recorded in it, to avoid any implied acceptance of the general regime, the Tax/IP treatment or the funds flow.
